relevance_reason: Reports a Chinese LDYT family with a novel causative MTND3 m.10197G>A mutation.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2009) described a Chinese family with 18 patients with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT), a mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.
quotes: In this paper, we describe a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients.
Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT) is a mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.

findings.statement: In affected members of a Chinese family with LDYT, Wang et al. (2009) identified a homoplasmic m.10197G>A mutation in the MTND3 gene, resulting in an ala47-to-thr substitution at a highly conserved residue, on a haplogroup D4b background. The mutation was found by resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome, and quantitative analysis showed homoplasmy in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. This was the first description of an ND3 mutation causing LDYT.
quotes: revealed a mutation (mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A)) substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3 on the background of haplogroup D4b
Quantitative analysis of the heteroplasmy of the mutation revealed a homoplasmy in the leukocytes of all the affected individuals on the maternal side.
This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2009) noted that the m.10197G>A MTND3 mutation had also been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome, and suggested that the clinical presentations associated with this mutation are wider, encompassing both LDYT and Leigh syndrome.
quotes: The mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation has recently been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.
These findings suggest that the clinical presentations associated with the mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation (ND3) are much wider, encompassing those of LDYT and Leigh syndrome.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2009) noted that LDYT had previously been attributed to mutations in the mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 genes, and identified MTND3 as an additional causative gene.
quotes: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with LHON and spastic dystonia caused by the mtDNA 3697G>A ND1 mutation, directly relevant to the LDYT phenotype.

findings.statement: Spruijt et al. (2007) reported a family in which Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and spastic dystonia occurred together. The authors noted that the family's clinical characteristics were similar to those of previously described families with LHON and dystonia carrying an ND6 mutation.
quotes: To report a novel mutation that is associated with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) within the same family affected by spastic dystonia.
This family has similar clinical characteristics as the previously described families with LHON and dystonia with an ND6 mutation.

findings.statement: In a patient with LHON from a family with LHON and spastic dystonia who did not carry 1 of the 3 primary LHON mutations, Spruijt et al. (2007) screened the complete mitochondrial DNA and identified a 3697G>A mutation in the ND1 gene. The heteroplasmy level was determined, and the mutation seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency. The authors concluded that the mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in this family, noted that it can also cause MELAS syndrome, and suggested that other genetic factors may contribute to clinical expression.
quotes: The complete mitochondrial DNA was screened for mutations in a patient with LHON without 1 of these 3 primary mutations. The heteroplasmy level and biochemical consequence of the mutation were determined.
A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.

This mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome (which encompasses mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke), and other genetic factors may contribute to the clinical expression.

findings.statement: Spruijt et al. (2007) found that the ND1 3697G>A mutation seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency in their family with LHON and spastic dystonia.
quotes: A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

relevance_reason: Reports a Japanese family with LHON and dystonia carrying the mtDNA G14459A (MTND6) mutation, which is the disorder this entry covers.

findings.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) described a Japanese family with generalized dystonia, attributed to striatal degeneration, that began in childhood, together with optic neuropathy of late onset.
quotes: We investigated a Japanese family with generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, which occurred in childhood, and late-onset optic neuropathy.

findings.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) sequenced the whole mitochondrial genome of the proband from a Japanese family with LHON and dystonia and found 42 nucleotide changes compared with the revised Cambridge Reference Sequence. One of them was the G14459A mutation in the NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 gene (MTND6), which was absent in 200 healthy Japanese controls. The authors noted that this mutation had previously been suggested to cause LHON and/or dystonia in Hispanic, African American, and Caucasian families. They stated that this was the first case of LHON with dystonia in which an mtDNA mutation had been found in a Japanese family.
quotes: We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.

The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
To our knowledge, this is the first case of LHON with dystonia that revealed a mtDNA mutation in a Japanese family.

findings.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) also found an A3203G mtDNA change in the proband. It was absent in 200 healthy Japanese controls, but its significance remained unknown.
quotes: We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese
The significance of the A3203G mutation remains unknown.

relevance_reason: Reports a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia, with mtDNA ND4 and ND6 mutations and a complex I deficiency.

findings.statement: De Vries et al. (1996) studied a large Dutch family with a rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) associated with hereditary spastic dystonia. Some family members had both neuropathy and ophthalmologic lesions, while others had only one of the two types of abnormality.
quotes: A rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) that is associated with hereditary spastic dystonia has been studied in a large Dutch family.
Neuropathy and ophthalmological lesions were present together in some family members, whereas only one type of abnormality was found in others.

findings.statement: In the Dutch family with LHON and dystonia, De Vries et al. (1996) found none of the mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON. Sequencing of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes identified a heteroplasmic A-to-G transition at nucleotide 11696 in the ND4 gene, which resulted in a val312-to-ile substitution.
quotes: mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON were not present.
A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.

findings.statement: In the same Dutch family, De Vries et al. (1996) also identified a homoplasmic T-to-A transition at nucleotide 14596 in the ND6 gene, which resulted in an ile26-to-met substitution.
quotes: A second mutation, a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene, resulted in the substitution of a methionine for the isoleucine at amino acid residue 26.

findings.statement: De Vries et al. (1996) found a severe complex I deficiency in a muscle biopsy from the family. They concluded that this provided a link between the mtDNA mutations and the complex phenotype that included Leber optic neuropathy.
quotes: Biochemical analysis of a muscle biopsy revealed a severe complex I deficiency, providing a link between these unique mtDNA mutations and this rare, complex phenotype including Leber optic neuropathy.

phenotypes.text: severe complex I deficiency in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

relevance_reason: This paper reports the family and the mtDNA ND6 m.14459G>A mutation that define Leber optic atrophy and dystonia.

findings.statement: Jun et al. (1994) studied a 5-generation Hispanic family in which members had maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON), early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions, or both.
quotes: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions was studied.

findings.statement: Jun et al. (1994) found that LHON and/or dystonia in the 5-generation Hispanic family were transmitted maternally.
quotes: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia

findings.statement: Jun et al. (1994) amplified buffy coat mtDNA from a severely affected child by PCR and sequenced more than 90% of it. The mtDNA belonged to Native American haplogroup D and differed from the Cambridge sequence at 40 positions. One of these, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 in the ND6 gene, changed a moderately conserved alanine to valine at residue 72 (A72V). The variant was absent from 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs and from 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, and 99 African mtDNAs. All 6 maternal relatives tested, across 3 generations, carried the mutation. One female relative with LHON was heteroplasmic. The authors suggested that this was the disease-causing mutation.
quotes: One of these variants, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459, changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72.
The np 14459 variant was not found in any of 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs, nor was it detected in 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, or 99 African mtDNAs.
Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation, with one female affected with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy being heteroplasmic.

variants.as_reported: G-to-A transition at np 14459, alanine to valine at ND6 residue 72

findings.population: Hispanic; Native American haplogroup D mtDNA

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It describes familial holotopistic striatal necrosis, a pathological finding that relates to the striatal lesions in this entry. With no abstract or full text, no patient, family or genetic details can be taken from it.

findings.statement: Miyoshi et al. (1969) reported familial holotopistic striatal necrosis.
quotes: Familial holotopistic striatal necrosis.

relevance_reason: This paper reports the original kindred in which Leber hereditary optic neuropathy occurs together with progressive generalized dystonia and transmission compatible with maternal inheritance.

findings.statement: Novotny et al. (1986) studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber disease, 14 had progressive generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, and 1 had both disorders.
quotes: We studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease; 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration; and 1 had both disorders.

findings.statement: In the kindred studied by Novotny et al. (1986), the mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission. The authors suggested that this neurologic disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.
quotes: The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission. This neurologic disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.

relevance_reason: This is the original description of familial dystonia with visual failure and striatal lucencies (Marsden syndrome), the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Marsden et al. (1986) described 7 members of 2 families with dystonia that was variably associated with subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy. CT scans showed striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies, especially in the putamen.
quotes: A unique disorder is described in seven members of two families in whom dystonia was variably associated with subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy, and striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen.

phenotypes.text: bilateral symmetrical putaminal lucencies on CT

findings.statement: Marsden et al. (1986) suggested that the disorder could be a variant of Leigh disease, but noted considerable differences from pathologically proven Leigh disease. They stated that the condition must be excluded in all patients thought to have idiopathic dystonia, subacute visual failure resembling Leber optic neuropathy, or both.
quotes: It is possible that this is a variant of Leigh's disease. However, there were considerable differences between these patients and those with pathologically proven Leigh's disease.
This condition must be excluded in all patients thought to have idiopathic dystonia, subacute visual failure similar to Leber's optic neuropathy, or a combination of these disorders.
